red.title: The cap table counts an $8.0M seed. The signed SAFEs add to $5.25M, and no Form D is on file.
red.ask: The cap table counts $8,000,000. The signed SAFEs add to $5,250,000. Who are the 9 unsigned commitments, when do they sign, and was a Form D filed after the first sale on 2026-02-17, under what name?
red.why: A round counted as closed should match the money that is signed and the filing the law asks for. When the cap table, the signed SAFEs and the public record disagree, the fund cannot be sure what it is buying into.

red.title: Gross margin counts cloud credits as free.

found.key: Found, cloud bill at full price

red.ask: Cloud credits paid $2,900 of September's $6,900 cloud bill, and they expire on 2027-03-31. What is gross margin at full price?
red.why: Cloud credits run out. A margin that holds only while the credits last shows less than it costs to serve each customer.

red.title: ARR counts a one-time log backfill as recurring revenue.

source.locator: 2026-09 rows, line is not Backfill overage

red.ask: September includes $3,800 for a one-time backfill of 38,000 GB. Can you show ARR without it, and how often do backfills recur?
red.why: ARR should count only revenue that repeats every year. A one-time backfill billed once inflates it, and every multiple built on ARR with it.

red.title: Runway leaves 2 of the 6 planned hires out of the burn.
red.ask: The model's burn carries 4 of the 6 hires in the hiring plan. What is runway with the full plan, and which hires would you hold?
red.why: The planned hires are the biggest new cost. A runway that leaves some of them out says the money lasts longer than it will.

reports.title: Traction and revenue

paras.body: Recurring revenue rose from $4,850 a month in 2026-06, the open-beta month, to $14,580 in 2026-09: 31 plan subscriptions, one enterprise contract and recurring usage over plan.

paras.lead: The backfill stays in its own line.
paras.body: A one-time backfill of 38,000 GB of old logs brought in $3,800 in September. One-time and variable charges go in their own line and are never multiplied by 12. Counted as recurring, they lift ARR to the deck's $221K.
32 teams pay out of 118 workspaces, and 21 of the 50 design partners. The deck says all 50 pay. Paying teams are the strong signal. Free design partners are interest.

paras.lead: The teams that pay stay and spend more.
paras.body: The teams paying in June pay more now: net revenue retention of 122.6%. Three months is a short record.

paras.lead: One customer is a large share.
paras.body: Corvane Systems pays 30.9% of recurring revenue. Depending on one customer is a concern even this early.

asks: The signed terms behind Corvane Systems, and when they renew.
Which design partners are expected to pay, and when.
Usage revenue by month, with recurring and one-time charges apart.

reports.title: Burn and runway

paras.body: September's spending was about $273,380: $4,000 of cloud after $2,900 of credits, $2,480 of model inference, and $266,900 for the team of 10 and everything else. Net of revenue, the company burns $255,000 a month.
The bank statements close September at $4,065,000, the cash the model uses.

paras.lead: Runway on the company's plan, and with every hire.
paras.body: At $255,000 a month, the cash lasts 15.9 months. The model's burn carries 4 of the 6 planned hires. With all of them, runway is 14.5 months.
Kimmy looks for 18 months of runway after a round closes. If the $2,750,000 of commitments without a signed SAFE comes in, runway with every hire is 23.8 months.
The $2,900 a month of credits stops after 2027-03-31. With that cost back and every hire, runway is 14.4 months.
